stem.text: The diagram shows a wire of diameter $D$ and length $L$ that is firmly clamped at one end between two blocks of wood. A load is applied to the wire which extends its length by $x$.

stem.alt: Diagram of a wire clamped at its top end between two blocks of wood, with a load hanging from its lower end. Printed labels: blocks of wood, wire, load.

stem.text: A second wire is made of the same material, but of diameter $2D$ and length $3L$. Both wires obey Hooke's law.
What is the extension of the second wire when the same load is applied?
